title: readIssueSystem regressed: throws on legacy `none` instead of normalizing to `local` (CAM-236 mandatory-alias violation)
description: CAM-236 (PR #171, v0.98.0) shipped a spec violation. The CAM-236 body made the `none`->`local` read-normalization a MANDATORY deprecated alias, not optional: mergeIntoConfig on init does NOT rewrite an existing project.toml value, so a raw rename silently breaks every already-initialized cam project whose project.toml still says issue_system="none" (ship-finalize.ts, ship-pr.ts close/stash gates, issue-list.ts). As shipped, src/config/issue-system.ts readIssueSystem THROWS on `none` (comment: 'Any other value including the legacy none sentinel -> throws') and the PR removed `none` from every code path. Regression to fix: (1) readIssueSystem must normalize none->local (accept `none` as deprecated alias, NOT throw); (2) cam init --issue-system arg validation must accept `none` as a deprecated alias; (3) scripts/build-release.sh smoke invokes `cam init --issue-system none` and now exits 1, which aborted the v0.98 --install. Restore `none` as a deprecated normalized-on-read alias per the original CAM-236 spec; KEEP --issue-system none in the smoke as a permanent regression guard. Severity CRITICAL: any existing cam project on issue_system="none" breaks on 0.98 ship/issue ops. Caught by build-release smoke; auditor APPROVE + reviewer CLEAN (3 rounds) both missed the mandatory-alias requirement.

acceptanceCriteria: readIssueSystem (src/config/issue-system.ts) normalizes the legacy value 'none' to 'local' and RETURNS 'local' (it must NOT throw on 'none'); truly-unknown values still throw fail-loud with the linear|github|local message.
cam init --issue-system arg validation accepts 'none' as a deprecated alias and writes issue_system='local' (or leaves it normalizable-on-read) so init does not crash on the legacy flag.
scripts/build-release.sh smoke keeps invoking `cam init --issue-system none` and the build --install completes (exit 0): the smoke is a permanent regression guard for the deprecated alias.

A unit test asserts readIssueSystem({issue_system:'none'}) === 'local'; git grep confirms no ===none gate remains broken (ship-finalize.ts, ship-pr.ts, issue-list.ts route 'none' the same as 'local' via the normalized read).
The value 'none' is NOT reintroduced as a canonical/selectable value: it is only a deprecated alias normalized on read. 'local' remains the canonical value and init default from CAM-236.
spec.scope: Restore the mandatory deprecated-alias behavior CAM-236 specified but PR #171 dropped. Touch src/config/issue-system.ts (normalize none->local on read instead of throw), cam init --issue-system arg validation (accept none alias), and scripts/build-release.sh (keep --issue-system none smoke as regression guard). Do not reintroduce none as a canonical value.
gotchas: mergeIntoConfig on init does NOT rewrite an existing project.toml value, so any already-initialized cam project still says issue_system='none'; a throw-on-none breaks ship-finalize/ship-pr/issue-list for all of them. This is exactly why the CAM-236 body called the alias mandatory, not optional.

The v0.98 binary is built in dist/ but NOT installed: the --install aborted when the build-release smoke (`cam init --issue-system none`) exited 1. The live binary and sidecar are still 0.97.0. After this fix ships, rebuild+install must succeed (smoke green) before hot-swapping the sidecar.

CAM-236 (PR #171) is merged and CAM-236 itself is still stage:specified/open on main because the 0.97 sidecar's post-merge issue-close choked on the new 'local' value; close CAM-236 with a 0.98+fix binary once this ships.

The regression escaped auditor APPROVE + reviewer CLEAN (3 rounds); only the build-release smoke caught it. The AC oracles for CAM-236 did not pin the none-alias behavior, so add an explicit oracle/test here.
domainTerms: deprecated alias: a legacy config value (none) that is still accepted on read and normalized to the canonical value (local), never surfaced as a selectable option nor written fresh.
readIssueSystem: the central project.toml reader (src/config/issue-system.ts) that selects the issue backend; fail-loud on unknown values, but must treat none as the local alias.
